comments:
The kube-apiserver processing flow is as follows, (non-critical paths are omitted)：

1. ... // other filters
2. [request_deadline_filter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97d40890d00acf721ecabb8c9a6fec3b3234b74b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/filters/request_deadline.go#L55) parse the http client timeout setting, sets the Ctx with Deadline in the http.Request
3. ...// other filters
4. [timeout_filter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97d40890d00acf721ecabb8c9a6fec3b3234b74b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L116) select the http.Request.Context().Done()

Pay attention to the processing logic in `timeout-filter`. Although the Context of http.Request has been cancelled, the Mutex on baseTimeoutWriter needs to be obtained between entering the [timeout](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97d40890d00acf721ecabb8c9a6fec3b3234b74b/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L226) function. The inner-handler may have written `http.Header`, ready to write `response.Body`, but the current code flow thinks that it should be Panic quickly, and it is recovered by [http2.runHandler](https://github.com/golang/net/blob/5f4716e94777e714bc2fb3e3a44599cb40817aac/http2/server.go#L2137) and sends http2.Reset to the Client. As a result, a `stream error: stream ID xxx; INTERNAL_ERROR` appears on the client side.

> If the time gap between the innerHandler processing time and the Client timeout setting is too small, this strange phenomenon will occur.
Currently seeing it in periodic and in presubmit for `TestWebhookTimeoutWithWatchCache`

> Currently seeing it in periodic and in presubmit for `TestWebhookTimeoutWithWatchCache`

Regardless of WithCache or WithoutCache, [the value of this Timeout setting](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9e5fcc49ec568f222a5274f443903d89fec3e591/test/integration/apiserver/admissionwebhook/timeout_test.go#L127) here is not reasonable.

review_comments:
I think https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/98797 is a more appropriate fix for the flake in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98606. 

When the inner handler is done it immediately writes `nil` to `resultCh` 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L105

Also, when we are inside the `timeout` function it means that we have already made a decision to send 504 for the request and the metrics has been recorded accordingly, see `postTimeoutFn`

If I misunderstood, please correct me. I think the timeout-handler will introduce uncertainty because of [the mutex here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2695ef3f1b0e2fc51ffb1bcb8491a4165587a089/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/filters/timeout.go#L226), which will cause the execution of this code to be divided into three cases

1.  If the inner-handler has not been processed yet (http.Header has not been wrote), it will send 504 and pre-defined by default The information is given to the client. 
2. If the inner-handler is processing, use panic to kill the underlying connection. 
3. if the inner-handler has already been processed. This PR is to increase the detection of this Case.
If I am not mistaken, this error check is outside the scope of this PR.
